article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Indica / 35% Sativa
Genetics: Bubble Gum × White Widow
Breeder: Soma Seeds
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: Typically low or trace
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Bubblegum, sweet candy, ripe fruit, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 10–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October into mid-November
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

White Light belongs to a period of cannabis breeding when the word “white” usually meant one thing: resin. Its flowers develop a pale green appearance beneath such dense trichome coverage that mature buds can look almost dusted in sugar, while their aroma travels in an entirely different direction. Instead of the sharp fuel or tropical candy common in newer weed, White Light can smell remarkably close to old-fashioned bubblegum, with ripe fruit, sweetness, skunk, citrus, and spice appearing underneath.

Soma Seeds created the cultivar from Bubble Gum and White Widow, two influential strains that shaped European marijuana during the 1990s and early 2000s. Soma described it as his most bubblegum-scented plant and emphasized both its candy flavor and unusually rich high. The cultivar is approximately 65% indica, yet its experience does not begin as pure sedation; cerebral euphoria arrives first before a deeper, increasingly comfortable body effect develops. Historical breeder material gives a lengthy 10–11-week flowering cycle, making patience essential despite the plant’s compact indica appearance.
Genetics and Lineage

White Light is Bubble Gum × White Widow, bred by Soma Seeds. Historical Soma material consistently lists the same pairing and describes the finished plant as 65% indica and 35% sativa. Bubble Gum contributes the unmistakable confectionery character. Its American roots eventually produced famous European selections valued for sweet fruit, chewing-gum aromas, and balanced hybrid effects. White Widow brings an entirely different strength to the pairing: tremendous resin production, compact flower formation, earthy spice, and the forceful potency that helped make it one of the defining Dutch cannabis cultivars of the 1990s.

The cross works because Soma did not allow the White Widow parent to erase Bubble Gum’s sweetness. Instead, the finished weed retains a pronounced bubblegum aroma while gaining the frosted appearance and dense flowers associated with White Widow. The breeder specifically warned growers not to harvest too early, noting that the strain needs approximately 10–11 weeks to develop its full character. Mature flowers become compact, pale green, and heavily coated with crystals.

A separate cultivar named White Light was later produced by Oregon Green Seed from White Widow × Amnesia Hashplant, so breeder attribution matters when researching the strain . The classic White Light covered here is the Soma Seeds Bubble Gum × White Widow version.
Effects and Experience

The high usually begins above the shoulders. A pleasant euphoric lift can arrive before the heavier indica character becomes obvious, improving mood and giving conversation, music, or entertainment a warmer quality. Rather than producing frantic sativa energy, the cerebral phase tends to feel soft and comfortable. Thoughts remain active but less urgent, creating an easy transition away from the demands of the day.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes more prominent. Warmth and heaviness can spread through the limbs while muscular tension fades, eventually producing the rich, deeply settled sensation Soma associated with the strain. Historical descriptions repeatedly advise getting comfortable before consuming it, which accurately captures the later stages. A sufficiently large dose may become sedating, making White Light better suited to late afternoon or evening than situations requiring sharp coordination.

Potency should be considered in historical context. Modern dispensary shelves routinely advertise marijuana above 25% THC, while older White Light references usually place the strain around the mid-to-upper teens. One long-term grower reported a laboratory result of 19.64% THC. That number does not make the cultivar weak; its dense resin and relaxing effect profile can still produce a substantial experience, particularly for consumers with limited tolerance.
Medical Benefits

White Light may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer cannabis that moves gradually from mood elevation into physical relaxation. The early euphoric period can temporarily shift attention away from everyday stress or emotional fatigue, while the later body component may appeal to people trying to unwind after prolonged physical tension. Its tendency toward drowsiness at larger doses also makes evening use more logical than morning use for many consumers.

Historical grower accounts have associated the cultivar with appetite stimulation, body comfort, and nighttime relaxation, but these experiences should not be treated as clinical evidence. Cannabis responses vary with dose, tolerance, cannabinoid concentration, consumption method, medications, and individual physiology.

White Light has not been clinically established as a treatment for pain, insomnia, anxiety, appetite disorders, or another medical condition. Medical consumers should use the cannabinoid analysis of the actual product whenever available and discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional when medical conditions or medications are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Bubblegum is the defining note. Soma considered White Light the most bubblegum-smelling cultivar in his collection, describing its flavor simply as candy. Well-cured flower can produce the unmistakable impression of sweet chewing gum mixed with overripe fruit, followed by skunk, spice, and a faint earthy backdrop. Grower reports from the strain’s earlier years also describe a strawberry-gum quality and exceptionally sweet aroma.

White Widow keeps that sweetness from becoming completely one-dimensional. Once the buds are broken apart, earthy cannabis, light citrus, herbs, and skunky spice become easier to identify. The inhale often emphasizes sugar and fruity gum, whereas the exhale develops more resinous, spicy, and slightly skunky qualities.

There is no reliable breeder-published laboratory terpene panel for the original Soma Seeds cultivar, so assigning precise dominant terpene percentages would overstate the evidence. This is an older strain developed before detailed terpene certificates became routine marketing material. Its sensory character is better documented through decades of breeder and grower descriptions than through a single standardized chemical profile.
Growing Information

White Light looks like a compact indica but asks for considerably more flowering time than its structure suggests. Soma’s original guidance places maturity around 10–11 weeks, with approximately 70 days commonly used as the practical indoor target. Harvesting too early sacrifices much of the resin development and richer final effect that distinguish properly matured flower.

Growth is sturdy and heavily branched. Historical cultivation reports describe plants that respond well to topping, supercropping, and screen-of-green techniques, producing numerous dense buds along strong side branches. Support can become useful during flowering as flowers gain weight. Compact indoor growth makes the cultivar manageable where ceiling height is limited, while larger outdoor plants can expand considerably when given unrestricted roots and strong sunlight.

The original Soma yield figure of 15–20 grams per plant sounds low by modern standards, but it referred to small-container cultivation rather than maximum production per square meter. Outdoor plants have considerably more potential when given a long season. Because the buds become hard and dense, airflow should remain a priority late in bloom. Outdoor harvest generally occurs in autumn, with historical references ranging from October toward mid-November depending on location and phenotype.
FAQ
What are the genetics of White Light?
The classic Soma Seeds White Light is Bubble Gum × White Widow. Soma listed the cultivar as approximately 65% indica and 35% sativa.
Is White Light indica or sativa?

White Light is an indica-dominant hybrid. Its effects typically begin with mild cerebral euphoria before the heavier physical relaxation associated with its indica side becomes increasingly noticeable.
How strong is White Light?

Historical references commonly place THC in approximately the 15–20% range, and one documented grower sample tested at 19.64% THC. Actual potency can vary with phenotype, environment, harvest maturity, and testing method.
What does White Light taste like?
Bubblegum and sweet candy dominate the flavor, accompanied by ripe fruit, skunk, citrus, earth, and spice. Soma specifically selected the cultivar for its pronounced bubblegum aroma.
How long does White Light take to flower?

Soma recommended approximately 10–11 weeks and specifically cautioned growers against harvesting it prematurely. Although individual plants may mature somewhat earlier, roughly 70 days is a useful target for the original genetics.
Final Thoughts on White Light

White Light reflects a period of cannabis history when combining two elite strains did not automatically mean creating another fruit-candy hybrid . Bubble Gum provides authentic chewing-gum sweetness and ripe fruit, while White Widow adds dense flower structure, powerful resin production, spice, and physical weight. The result is weed that smells unmistakably sweet yet finishes with enough skunk and earth to retain the personality of classic Dutch-era marijuana.

Its 10–11-week flowering period requires more patience than many modern indica hybrids, but that extra time allows the compact flowers to develop the pale, crystal-covered appearance responsible for the White Light name. The effects follow a similarly gradual progression, beginning with pleasant euphoria before settling into deeper physical relaxation and potential drowsiness. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in older Soma Seeds genetics, authentic bubblegum flavors, and heavily resinous flower from before the dominance of Cookies, Gelato, and Runtz, White Light remains an appealing example of classic European breeding built from two legendary parents.
